title: Make the mark-race test fail loudly when its interleaving does not happen
action: mark_pass_does_not_mark_a_session_whose_heartbeat_lands_before_the_lock (status_full/tests.rs:1546) holds the sessions lock so the mark pass's bounded retry must wait, sleeps 60ms, lands a fresh heartbeat, then releases. The interleaving it needs is: pre-check reads STALE, then the heartbeat lands, then the lock is acquired and the record re-read FRESH. If the spawned thread has not reached its pre-check within the 60ms, the heartbeat lands first, the pre-check sees a fresh record and skips, and the assertion still passes — green for the wrong reason, with the under-lock re-judgement never exercised. Make the test assert its own premise so that case fails loudly: have the spawned thread report completion through a channel, and before landing the heartbeat assert the pass has NOT finished, so a run where the pass raced ahead is a failure rather than a silent pass. Keep the existing outcome assertions. Do not touch production code — mark_stale_sessions and the lock helpers stay exactly as they are; this is a test-instrument fix, per the repo's own rule that a fixture must be shown to reach the branch its test names.

truths: The test fails when the mark pass completes before the heartbeat is landed, instead of passing
The existing assertions still hold: race1 is not marked and its record carries no status

artifacts.substantive: the test asserts the pass is still in flight before the heartbeat lands; no TODO stubs

key_links: the premise assertion runs before write_session_fixture lands the fresh heartbeat
prohibitions: No change to any lock helper

trace.outcome: The mark-race test asserts its own premise: the pass reports completion through a channel and the test fails loudly if it finished before the heartbeat landed. Proven by removal.
